name: Broken Tools
summary: At the dig northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven picks lie broken on the forge. Baine Bloodhoof wants proof that the excavation threatening Mulgore's land and wildlife has been stopped.

sections.title: Sabotaging the Dig
sections.body: Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven excavators dig into Mulgore's hills in search of ancient history. The tauren see their work as a defilement of the Earth Mother. The digging's noise and destruction agitate the local wildlife, especially the roaming kodo herds. Young Baine Bloodhoof orders defenders to take the prospectors' iron picks and break them at a forge. With their picks ruined, the expedition cannot gouge further into the earth.

faq.answer: Broken Tools are the ruined heads and splintered shafts of Prospector's Picks, taken from the dwarven excavators in Mulgore and crushed at a forge.

faq.q: Why does Baine Bloodhoof want them destroyed?
faq.answer: Baine believes digging into the soil defiles the land and angers Mulgore's wildlife, especially the kodos. Breaking the picks stops the excavation and warns that the land will not yield its wisdom to reckless digging.

faq.q: Where can these picks be broken?
faq.answer: You can break the picks at any working forge. One stands at the dwarven dig site, and others can be found in Bloodhoof Village or Thunder Bluff.

faq.q: Why are dwarves digging in Mulgore?
faq.answer: The dwarves believe Mulgore's soil holds deep secrets and relics of antiquity. Searching for their origins, they hollow out foreign lands without regard for the people who live there.

angles.text: As a tauren, bringing ruined tools to Baine helps defend the Earth Mother from digging that torments the native beasts.
As a blacksmith, you can turn your forge and anvil against dwarven ironwork to defend the land.
